open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos583

/--
A subgraph `H` of `G` is a path subgraph if it is the subgraph traced out by a path in `G`,
i.e. a walk with no repeated vertices.
-/
def IsPathSubgraph {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (H : G.Subgraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ (u v : V) (p : G.Walk u v), p.IsPath ∧ H = p.toSubgraph

/--
Every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\lceil n/2\rceil$
edge-disjoint paths.

A problem of Erdős and Gallai.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_583 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) :
    ∃ D : Finset G.Subgraph,
      (∀ H ∈ D, IsPathSubgraph H) ∧
      IsDecomposition G D ∧
      D.card ≤ ⌈(Fintype.card V : ℚ) / 2⌉₊ := by
  sorry

end Erdos583

reformulations.difference: The witness is a finset of path subgraphs and may include zero-edge, single-vertex paths, whereas an edge-set partition conventionally omits empty parts.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: IsDecomposition is equivalent to requiring that every edge of G belongs to exactly one member of D. Filtering D to retain only subgraphs with nonempty edge sets preserves this property and the path condition, and cannot increase D.card. Conversely, a decomposition with nonempty parts is already an allowed witness. Both the unique-edge characterization and the equivalence of the bounded existence statements with and without empty-edge pieces were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully express the source mathematics. The finite simple undirected graph domain, connectedness hypothesis, simple-path condition, edge-disjoint coverage, quantifier scope and rational ceiling bound all match. The source still records the problem as open. Lean checks covered empty and singleton vertex types, explicit K2 and K3 decompositions, non-induced paths, reversal, rejection of repeated-vertex walks and cycles, and ceiling values for n = 0 through 8. Background-only references CFZ26, DeKo00, Fa02, Lo68 and Py96 could not be read directly because of access failures; Ch78 was obtained as an image-only PDF without extractable text. Their relevant results were read in the source-page summaries, while the file's actual declarations were independently verified against the accessible primary papers.
